newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Bangui army mutineers start return to barracks.
newsitem.headline: Bangui army mutineers start return to barracks.

text.p: Army mutineers in the Central African Republic began a return to barracks on Friday under a new commander as part of a process of national reconciliation.
After three mutinies in under a year, several hundred men from the Mixed Intervention Regiment held a symbolic ceremony at their Kassai barracks stronghold in the capital Bangui.
Prime Minister Michel Gbezera-Bria represented President Ange-Felix Patasse at the ceremony, which was also attended by Mali's former army ruler and mediator Amadou Toumani Toure.
"This ceremony is within the framework of the process of national reconciliation," the mutineers' leader, Captain Anicet Saulet, said during the ceremony.
"Today's ceremony aims to launch the process of reintegrating our forces back in the barracks," the mutineers' spokesman Lieutenant Parfait Mbay told Reuters.
The first mutinies last April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a northern civilian who won 1993 presidential elections.
The third, which began on November 15, degenerated into ethnic bloodshed. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order and handed over to African peacekeepers.

Toumani Toure brokered a January 25 peace plan after clashes between mutineers and French troops but mutual suspicion between the southern mutineers and Patasse loyalists in the presidential guard has soured the atmosphere.
Tension persisted and erupted in clashes with the peacekeepers in March before peace moves resumed.
